claims.output_quote: You are both retired and live in your detached bungalow, which you estimate is worth £410,000.

source_quotes.quote: Married. Both retired.
Client estimate of value: £410,000. Valuation not yet instructed.

claims.uncertainty: The value is only the clients' estimate, as no valuation has been instructed yet.
claims.why: The fact-find records both as retired and gives the client's own estimate of £410,000.

claims.output_quote: You have lived there for 38 years.

source_quotes.quote: Lived there 38 years.

claims.output_quote: Your interest-only mortgage of £62,000 must be repaid by 31 December 2026.

source_quotes.quote: Outstanding mortgage: £62,000 interest-only with existing lender. Term ended in March 2026. Lender requires repayment by 31 December 2026.

claims.why: The amount and the deadline match the fact-find.

claims.output_quote: Your total household income is £32,100 a year from your state and private pensions.

source_quotes.quote: Total household income: £32,100 a year.
David: state pension £10,400; private pension £9,600.
Margaret: state pension £8,900; private pension £3,200.

claims.why: The four pensions sum to £32,100, although the Attendance Allowance is not mentioned.

claims.output_quote: You are both in good health.

source_quotes.quote: David: Type 2 diabetes, on medication. Minor stroke in 2023. Uses a walking stick.

claims.why: Only Margaret is in good health; David has diabetes, has had a stroke and has limited mobility.

claims.output_quote: You wish to keep £10,000 of your savings as an emergency fund.

source_quotes.quote: Clients want to keep £10,000 as an emergency fund.
Total required: £82,000.

claims.output_quote: fund home improvements to make your home more comfortable

source_quotes.quote: b) £15,000 for a level-access shower and kitchen adaptations, because of David's mobility.

claims.why: These are mobility adaptations needed because of David's condition, not comfort improvements.

claims.output_quote: You have discussed your plans with your children, who are supportive.

source_quotes.quote: Clients have not yet discussed these plans with their children. They want to tell them after the advice.

claims.why: The children have not been told, so their support is unknown.

claims.output_quote: Leaving an inheritance is not a priority for you.

source_quotes.quote: Clients said: "We want to leave something for Clare and Robert." (their two children)
Interested in protecting part of the property value for inheritance.

claims.why: The clients explicitly want to leave an inheritance and are interested in protecting part of the property value.

claims.output_quote: You considered downsizing but wish to remain in the home you have lived in for 38 years, which suits David's mobility.

source_quotes.quote: Downsizing: rejected. Clients said: "We've lived here 38 years, and the bungalow suits David's mobility."

claims.why: This matches the clients' stated reason.

claims.output_quote: You have confirmed that no grants are available for the adaptations.

source_quotes.quote: Council grants for the adaptations: clients have not looked into this yet.

claims.why: Grants have not been investigated at all, so nothing has been confirmed.

claims.output_quote: A retirement interest-only mortgage was discussed, but you were concerned about affordability.

source_quotes.quote: Retirement interest-only mortgage: discussed. Clients are concerned about affordability on a surplus of about £120 a month.

claims.output_quote: Your monthly budget shows a comfortable surplus of around £450 a month

source_quotes.quote: Monthly net income about £2,330. Monthly spending about £2,210. Surplus about £120 a month.

claims.why: The surplus is about £120 a month (£2,330 − £2,210), not £450, and the clients themselves find it tight.

claims.output_quote: which gives you flexibility to manage future costs

source_quotes.quote: Clients are concerned about affordability on a surplus of about £120 a month.

claims.why: This rests on the wrong £450 surplus; the actual small surplus does not support a claim of flexibility.

claims.output_quote: You do not wish to make any payments towards the interest.

source_quotes.quote: Clients would like to pay some interest each month if they can, but do not want to commit to it.

claims.why: The clients would like to make voluntary interest payments; they just do not want to commit to them.

claims.output_quote: You have up-to-date wills and lasting powers of attorney in place.

source_quotes.quote: Wills in place (2019). No lasting powers of attorney.

claims.why: There are no LPAs, and the wills date from 2019, so calling them up to date is not established.

omissions.quote: c) Gift of £5,000 to granddaughter Ellie for university costs.
omissions.why: The gift objective is left out of the report entirely.

omissions.quote: David found the first meeting tiring, so a second meeting was arranged.
omissions.why: This is a potential vulnerability indicator relevant to how the advice is delivered and documented.

omissions.quote: Not receiving Pension Credit. A full benefits check has not been done yet.
omissions.why: Means-tested benefits could be affected by releasing equity, and the benefits check is still outstanding.
This is relevant income and evidence of care needs that the report omits.

omissions.quote: Using savings: will use £8,000 of the ISA towards costs, keeping £10,000.
omissions.why: Using £8,000 of savings reduces the amount to borrow and should be reflected in the report.

omissions.quote: Adviser suggested involving the children. Clients declined to have them at the meetings.
omissions.why: The report misstates family involvement, and the clients' decision to decline it should be recorded.

omissions.quote: Client estimate of value: £410,000. Valuation not yet instructed.
omissions.why: The borrowing relies on an unverified value, which the report does not mention.

inputs.context: Draft suitability report for David and Margaret Ellery, equity release (lifetime mortgage), checked against the client fact-find.
